title: Hardware-normalized performance ledger and publishable profile artifact
creator: Amira Chen
description: Goal: Design and deliver a publishable, hardware-normalized performance ledger for newly onboarded models. The ledger is a signed artifact (profile.json + signatures) that expresses latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/s under standard batching shapes), and unit cost normalized to canonical hardware equivalents and regional pricing. This work defines the schema, normalization math, publishing CLI, and the operational gating rules for canary and full publish. It also ties a profile to a model pin and provides rollback metadata.
background_and_rationale: Existing verified profiles vary by hardware and region; teams currently must manually interpret per-GPU numbers when selecting a runtime or when routing requests. We need a single published artifact that: 1) makes cross-hardware comparisons explicit via normalization factors, 2) includes cost-per-1k-tokens normalized to a canonical baseline, and 3) stores deterministic fingerprints + git-backed provenance to speed safe rollouts across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A signed 'performance-ledger' JSON artifact is produced by the onboarding pipeline for each verified model version.
2) Ledger contains: canonical_latency_percentiles (p50/p95/p99), canonical_tokens_per_sec (batch shapes), canonical_cost_per_1k_tokens, hardware_normalization_table, region_cost_adjustment_factors, model_pin reference, artifact_fingerprint (sha256), and publish_timestamp.
3) CLI: redwood profile publish --artifact <file> that validates signatures and pushes to git-backed registry.
4) Console and API surfaces can fetch ledger and display normalized cost and latency for chosen hardware/region.
5) Canary publish flow implemented: staging -> 5% shadow -> 25% shadow -> full publish with automated pass/fail checks on sampled traffic and quality gates.
6) Rollback procedure: automated revert that re-pins previous artifact and records rollback reason in ledger history.
out_of_scope: Per-model microbench harnesses (infra team will own microbench infra ticket). Deep ML model architecture changes to improve latency numbers (research will raise separate PRDs). Region-level pricing contract negotiation with cloud vendors.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Normalization math over-simplifies real-world differences -> Mitigation: include raw per-hardware samples and percentile offsets in ledger so runtime can apply conservative adjustments.
Risk: Cost normalization becomes stale when cloud prices change -> Mitigation: include price_timestamp and small TTL; schedule automated re-eval job (separate ticket) and surface warnings in Console.
Risk: Signoff friction between PM/Eng/Security -> Mitigation: automate signature generation with CI and include security_signoff_required flag in publish pipeline (toggleable).
implementation_notes: Schema will follow JSON-LD lite for future extensibility; ledger fields will be strongly typed in CI. Hardware normalization uses anchored multiplier factors derived from co-located microbench runs and an L2 smoothing function to avoid outlier-driven jumps. Cost normalization uses canonicalSkuCost * tokens_per_sec / 1000 with region multipliers pulled from pricing table keyed by cloud provider and region id.
telemetry_contract: Publish artifact must include sampled latency histograms (raw p50/p95/p99 by hardware) and synthetic throughput numbers; onboarding pipeline will emit metrics: profile_publish_attempts, profile_publish_success, publish_latency_seconds, and publish_validation_failures with tags {model, model_version, hardware_anchor, region}. Dashboard will show publish success rate and recent regressions.
canary_and_rollout_plan: 1) Publish to 'staging' registry only and validate artifact signature. 2) Wire 5% shadow traffic in a non-customer-affecting namespace and verify traffic-level latency/throughput within bounded delta vs ledger. 3) If pass, expand to 25% shadow and run quality evals on golden prompt samples. 4) On success, mark ledger as 'published' and update model pin. 5) If any step fails, auto-revert to previous ledger and open ENG ticket with diagnostic logs.
